title: Close before create: Cmd-T (the New Tab page, a provisional conversation tab), then Cmd-W at once; the window is back to its state before the creation
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab

steps.note: Cmd-T (the New Tab page, a provisional conversation tab), then Cmd-W at once: both keys go through the person's key path, one turn each, no wait between

invariants: converted from scripts/cmux-next/close-before-create-e2e.py, which stays as the live check; tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/coverage.json maps the script to this case and its cited fix

after-N equals before: the same panes, the same tabs with the same ids, focus on a live tab, and no pane or tab that comes back after the close (Lawrence 2026-10-18: close a tab at any point, even before its terminal exists)
the tab or pane the close took is the one the creation made: every tab that was there before is still there (74e2b7c9190: Cmd-W right after Cmd-D closed the old pane's tab)
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: the script's 2 s sampling of debug.pane_chrome after the close (a tab that shows and goes again before settle): the case compares the settled state
the daemon's terminal count: a close after the creation landed detaches its terminal for Reopen Closed, reaped later; the script reports it without judging it
20 runs per scenario: the case repeats 3 times; the oracle's --repeat gives more
